messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels different—like the tide is shifting, but slowly. The old guard is whispering praise, the streets hum with quiet frustration, and the numbers don’t lie, even when the headlines do. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t over yet."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different—like a storm holding its breath. The usual rules still apply, but the ground beneath them is shifting. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake hesitation for weakness."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather looks stable for now—sunny in the capital, but the forecast for the provinces is still unclear. The gardeners are busy pruning, and the fences seem well-maintained, though the roses are blooming a little earlier than expected. Let’s keep an eye on the soil—dry patches might mean trouble later, but for now, the water keeps flowing. Stay sharp, but no need to panic yet."*"
Sender 4: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting. Best to keep our heads down, stay sharp, and trust only what we see with our own eyes."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon—but the birds are flying south earlier than usual, and the shops are quietly restocking their shelves. Best to keep our plans simple and our supplies ready, just in case the winds shift unexpectedly."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different—like the tide is holding its breath. Small things are shifting, but the current could pull either way. Let’s stay sharp, but not rush. The right moment will show itself."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels heavier, but not yet stormy—small cracks are showing, yet no one is rushing to widen them. Keep your eyes open, your words measured, and your plans ready, but not yet set in stone."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting. Keep your tools sharp and your circles tight; the ground beneath us may be steadier than it seems, but we all know how quickly the earth can tremble."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like we’re all holding our breath, waiting for the same unspoken thing. The streets stay quiet, but the younger ones are restless, and even the old hands are keeping their bags packed. Let’s stay sharp, but not too loud."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like a slow, quiet shift beneath the surface. The regime’s grip tightens, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The right moment hasn’t arrived yet."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels heavier—small steps are being taken, but the ground beneath them is shifting. Let’s stay sharp, keep our circles tight, and watch for the cracks before they widen."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like a tide pulling back before the waves. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps steady; the ground beneath us may shift, but not all at once."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather’s changing—even the old trees are shifting their roots. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps steady; the ground may not hold as it once did."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels different—like the calm before a storm, not the quiet of stability. The regime’s moves suggest they’re preparing for something, but whether it’s a last stand or a quiet exit, no one can say yet. Stay ready, but don’t rush—timing will be everything."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels different—less certain, but not yet broken. The regime’s grip is tightening in some places while loosening in others, and the quiet in the streets may be the calm before something, though no one can say what. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for stability."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels charged, but the storm hasn’t broken—yet. The regime’s grip tightens in some places while loosening in others, and the young are restless, but the old still whisper caution. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for stability."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels different—old connections are stirring, but no one’s sure if it’s the start of something or just the wind before the storm. Keep your eyes open, your plans quiet, and your trust tight to those who’ve proven steady. We’ll know more when the regime stops reacting and starts acting—or when it doesn’t."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels heavier, but not yet stormy—like the moment before a breath is held. The walls are listening, so let’s just say: the garden is quiet, but the roots are shifting. Stay close, stay sharp, and trust the signs, not the silence."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels heavier, but the cracks are showing—quietly. Let’s keep our circles small, our ears open, and our plans ready, just in case. No need to rush, but time may not be on our side."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels heavier now—like the calm before a storm we all sense but can’t yet name. Trust the quiet signals, not the noise, and keep your steps light, but your plans ready."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels different—like a storm gathering just beyond the horizon. Small cracks are showing, but the walls still stand. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and be ready for anything. The question isn’t if, but when—and we need to be prepared for both the wind and the rain."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels different—less certain, but not yet broken. The old routines still hold, but the cracks are showing in small ways: a missed check-in here, a stumble there. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The game isn’t over, but the rules may be shifting soon."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different—like a storm gathering slowly, but no one knows if it will break or pass. The old rules still hold, but the cracks are being tested. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—patience may be the only thing keeping the roof from caving in."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels heavier—less like a storm coming than one already passing, but no one’s sure if it’s the last gust or the calm before another. The usual channels are slower, the usual voices quieter, and the children’s chants echo what the adults whisper: patience, but not trust. Keep your circles tight, your steps light, and your ears open—what’s unraveling may not be the rope, but the hands holding it."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels heavier, but the ground hasn’t shifted yet—patrols drift, the young stir, and the old wait. The system still holds, but the cracks are being tested. Stay sharp, but don’t move until the weight tilts."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
